# Module checks and releases

The shared [PR check](./pr-check.yml) discovers affected modules and runs their checks when a PR is opened, reopened or updated. Add the `PR: Run E2E Tests` label when deployment tests are needed for a same-repository PR. Fork PRs do not run deployment tests through this label; coordinate an authorized run with a maintainer.

The planned shared `Avm.Authoring` script using `gh` will hand off a fork PR to a same-repository release branch. An authorized Microsoft FTE's invocation will authorize the handoff, with no extra approval or confirmation prompt. Security-review the fork changes before invoking the script with privileged credentials. Existing GitHub branch protections, required reviews and checks remain in force. Until the script is implemented and released, coordinate the handoff with a maintainer; no script command is available here yet.

The shared [release workflow](./release.yml) runs on pushes to `main` or can be started manually. Push runs select module roots with changed compiled templates or versions in that push; manual runs discover pending releases from tag history. Both check the changelog and require approval through `publish-approval` before creating scoped release tags. Registry publication is a separate process, so verify the published version after the tag is created.

For a manual retry, run the workflow from `main` and optionally set `targetCommit` to a full lowercase 40-character commit SHA from upstream `main` history. Blank uses the triggering commit. The selected SHA is used for checkout, release discovery and tag creation; pending changes are compared with each module's latest remote release tag, not the current `main` tip. Already-released changes are skipped, and a release tag that is not ancestral to the selected SHA causes the run to fail rather than publish an outdated revision.

For local authoring and checks, install `Avm.Authoring` from MAR using the [Bicep prerequisites](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/contributing/bicep/prerequisites/) and follow the [local validation guide](https://azure.github.io/Azure-Verified-Modules/contributing/bicep/bicep-contribution-flow/validate-bicep-module-locally/).
